cards.text: The writer of this letter is talking to people who share the same fathers he does, and he dives right in about how God talks to His people. Long ago, God spoke to those fathers many times and in many different ways.

cards.question: True or false: long ago, God spoke to the fathers through the prophets.

cards.text: Then the letter turns a corner, because in these last days God has spoken in a new way. It's like getting messages relayed through three coworkers for years, and then finally hearing it face to face.

cards.question: In these last days, who has God spoken to us by?

cards.text: That Son is Jesus, the Son of God (Hebrews 4:14). And He isn't just a messenger: God appointed Him heir of all things.

cards.question: True or false: the letter says God made the universe through the Son.

cards.text: The Son is the radiance of God's glory and the exact representation of His nature. I'm a stamper, friend, and EXACT is a word I could only dream about back in that drawer.

cards.question: By His powerful word, what is the Son upholding?

cards.text: ALL things, and I need my whole mustache just to hold up ONE cookie box. Then the writer tells what the Son did about sins.

cards.question: The Son provided ___ for sins.
After He provided purification for sins, what did the Son do?

answers.text: Sat down at the right hand of the Majesty
Stood guard at the gates of heaven
Went back to speaking through the prophets

cards.text: Now the writer brings in the angels. I've met one, friend, and I spent the whole time squinting into the light asking if he had the right drawer.

cards.question: True or false: the writer puts the Son on the same level as the angels.

cards.text: He became as far superior to the angels as the name He has inherited is excellent beyond theirs. FAR above, friend, and the next lines show why.
Now the writer shows the Son is above the angels, and the proof starts with a question. To which of the angels did God ever say, "You are My Son; today I have become Your Father"?

cards.question: The writer asks which angel God ever said "You are My Son" to. What answer is the writer expecting?

cards.text: Then comes another line: "I will be His Father, and He will be My Son". And when God brings His firstborn into the world, He says something about all His angels.

cards.question: When God brings His firstborn into the world, He says to let all God's angels ___ Him.

cards.text: Now here's what God says about the angels themselves: He makes them winds and flames of fire. Flames of FIRE, friend, and I get excited when my oven hits 350.

cards.question: In that line about winds and flames of fire, what else does God call His angels?

cards.text: But about the Son, God says something completely different. He speaks to the Son and calls Him "O God".

cards.question: True or false: God says the Son's throne will last only for a season.
In God's words, justice is the scepter of the Son's kingdom, and the Son has loved ___ and hated wickedness.

cards.text: Therefore God anointed the Son above His companions with the oil of joy. The oil of JOY, friend, and for years the only thing anybody poured on me was dust.
Still talking about the Son, the writer goes all the way back to the beginning, when the Lord laid the foundations of the earth.

cards.question: True or false: in the line about the Lord laying the foundations of the earth, the heavens are called the work of the Lord's hands.

cards.text: Then the line says they will perish and all wear out like a garment. Friend, I KNOW about wearing out: my edges went soft and my lines went blurry.

cards.question: The heavens wear out like a garment. What does the line say about the Son?

cards.text: He'll roll them up like a robe, but His years will never end. Then the writer asks the angel question again: which angel did God ever tell, "Sit at My right hand"?

cards.question: God tells the Son to sit at His right hand until He makes the Son's ___ a footstool for His feet.

cards.text: So what are the angels? The writer calls them ministering spirits, sent to serve, and the one at my drawer said, "I've been sent," while I'm lying under three takeout menus going, "Sent... for ME?"

cards.question: Who does the writer say the angels are sent to serve?

answers.text: The kings of the whole earth
The priests serving in the temple

cards.text: Now the writer turns all that teaching into a warning. We must pay closer attention to what we have heard.

cards.question: True or false: the writer says to pay closer attention so that we do not drift away.

cards.text: Drifting sneaks up on you, friend, like zoning out on the highway and looking up THREE exits past yours. Then the writer looks back at the message spoken by angels.

cards.question: The writer says the message spoken by angels was ___.

cards.text: Back then, every transgression and disobedience received its just punishment. So how could we ever escape if we neglect such a great salvation?

cards.question: True or false: the writer is saying there's still a way out for anyone who neglects this great salvation.

cards.text: And this salvation is no rumor, friend. It was first announced by the Lord Himself.

cards.question: After the Lord announced this salvation, who confirmed it to the writer and the readers?

cards.text: Then God affirmed it too. And friend, as a stamper, NOBODY loves a good stamp of approval more than me.

cards.question: How did God affirm this salvation?

answers.text: Through signs and wonders and miracles
Through a new temple and new laws
Through angels speaking from the clouds

cards.text: And there's one more way God affirmed it: gifts of the Holy Spirit.

cards.question: True or false: the gifts of the Holy Spirit were handed out to whoever asked first.

findings.problem: The story card only says that the Son did something about sins; it gives no basis for supplying "purification." This blank asks for the unseen wording of Hebrews 1:3 rather than a meaning established by the walkthrough.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: Card 3 says only that God says something about all His angels. Asking for "worship" therefore makes the baker guess the next word of Hebrews 1:6.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: Hebrews 1:8 says that the Son's throne endures forever and ever, but no card states that fact. Marking "only for a season" false merely rejects one invented duration and leaves this important description of the Son's throne untaught.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: The preceding story card stops at God calling the Son "O God" and does not establish the contrast between righteousness and wickedness. The blank asks for the unseen wording of Hebrews 1:9.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: The right answer, "He remains the same," is stated in Hebrews 1:12. Hebrews 1:11 supplies only the question's setup about wearing out, so the choice citation Hebrews 1:11-12 is wider than the verses of its right answer.

rule.text: Cite exactly what the card uses. Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower. A choice card cites only the verses of its right answer.

findings.problem: Card 15 quotes only "Sit at My right hand." Nothing in the earlier cards introduces the enemies and footstool picture, so this blank asks the baker to guess how Hebrews 1:13 continues.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: Card 3 merely says that the writer looks back at the message spoken by angels. The punishment that supports calling it "binding" is not introduced until card 5, so this blank is an uninformed guess at unseen wording.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: Hebrews 2:4 says that the gifts of the Holy Spirit were distributed according to God's will, but no card teaches that positive detail. Marking "whoever asked first" false only rules out one invented method, and the walkthrough ends without covering the last part of the verse.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.
